subject: The World Around Us
title: Ravi's Family
hook: Learn about family members and how they care for each other.

characters.name: Papa
characters.role: father who works and plays cricket

slides.title: My Family
slides.storyContext: Ravi sits with Dadi in the kitchen while she makes dal and rice.
slides.inSimpleWords: Family is the people we live with and love most.

image.alt: My Family — My Family

slides.title: Ravi Learns About Family
slides.storyContext: Ravi asks Dadi: 'Dadi, who is in my family?' Dadi smiles and starts counting on her fingers. 'Let me show you, beta. There's me, your Papa, your Mummy, your sister Priya, and you. We all live together and take care of each other.'
slides.inSimpleWords: A family is a group of people who live together and love each other.

image.alt: Ravi Learns About Family — My Family

slides.title: Parents
slides.storyContext: Papa comes home from work and lifts Ravi high in the air. Mummy makes his favorite aloo paratha. 'Your Mummy and Papa are your parents,' Dadi explains. 'They take care of you, feed you, and love you very much.'

points.label: Who are parents?
points.text: Your Mummy and Papa are your parents. They love you and take care of you.

points.label: What do parents do?
points.text: They give you food, clothes, shelter, and teach you good things.

slides.inSimpleWords: Parents are Mummy and Papa who love and care for you.

image.alt: Parents — My Family

slides.title: Grandparents
slides.storyContext: Dadi and Dadu sit on the verandah every evening. Dadi tells Ravi old stories about when Papa was a little boy. Dadu teaches him to count in Hindi.

points.label: Dadi and Dadu
points.text: Your grandparents are your parents' Mummy and Papa.

points.label: They help
points.text: Grandparents tell stories, give hugs, and help take care of you.

slides.inSimpleWords: Grandparents are older family members who love and teach us.

image.alt: Grandparents — My Family

slides.title: Brothers and Sisters
slides.storyContext: Ravi's sister Priya takes his hand and walks with him to school. On the way, they count cars and buses. Priya helps him carry his school bag. After school, they play with marbles and top in the courtyard.

points.label: Who are siblings?
points.text: Your brothers and sisters are your siblings. They are part of your family.

points.label: Why do we love them?
points.text: Siblings play with us, help us, and we share our toys and food with them.

slides.inSimpleWords: Siblings are your brothers and sisters who are born to the same parents.

image.alt: Brothers and Sisters — My Family

slides.title: Uncles and Aunts
slides.storyContext: On Sunday, Ravi's Uncle (Chacha) and Aunt (Chachi) visit. Chacha plays cricket with Ravi in the park and buys him sugarcane juice. Chachi brings sweets and hugs everyone.

points.label: Who are uncles and aunts?
points.text: They are your parents' brothers and sisters.

points.label: They care too
points.text: Uncles and aunts love you, play with you, and give you gifts.

slides.inSimpleWords: Uncles and aunts are your parents' siblings who are part of your extended family.

image.alt: Uncles and Aunts — My Family

slides.title: Cousins
slides.storyContext: Ravi's cousin Arjun is also at Chacha's house. Arjun is about the same age. They play with toy cars, climb trees, and eat mango ice-cream together. 'Arjun is your cousin,' Papa tells Ravi. 'You are family because your parents and his parent are siblings.'

points.label: What is a cousin?
points.text: Your cousin is the child of your uncle or aunt.

points.label: Friends and family
points.text: Cousins are your relatives and often become your best friends.

slides.inSimpleWords: Cousins are the children of your uncles and aunts.

image.alt: Cousins — My Family

slides.title: Ravi's Whole Family
slides.storyContext: At Diwali, Ravi's whole family comes together. Dadi counts everyone: 'Ravi, Priya, Papa, Mummy, me, Dadu, Chacha, Chachi, Arjun, and Arjun's sister Neha.' Everyone eats khir together and lights diyas.

example.problem: Ravi draws his family tree. He writes: Parents (Mummy and Papa), Grandparents (Dadi and Dadu), Sister (Priya), Uncle (Chacha), Aunt (Chachi), Cousins (Arjun and Neha). How many people are in Ravi's immediate family at home?
example.solution: Ravi counts: Ravi + Priya + Papa + Mummy + Dadi + Dadu = 6 people live together in Ravi's home.

slides.inSimpleWords: Family includes all the people we live with and love: parents, grandparents, and siblings.

image.alt: Ravi's Whole Family — My Family

slides.title: Who Is Who in Your Family?
slides.storyContext: Dadi asks Ravi: 'Can you name all the people in our family and say what they mean to you?' Ravi closes his eyes and thinks of everyone he loves.

example.problem: Name 5 people in your family and draw what each one does that makes you happy.
example.solution: Sample answer: 1. Mummy - makes food I like, 2. Papa - plays with me, 3. Priya - helps me, 4. Dadi - tells stories, 5. Chacha - buys me treats.

slides.inSimpleWords: Think about your family and remember that each person loves you in their own way.

image.alt: Who Is Who in Your Family? — My Family

slides.title: What We Learned

points.text: Family is a group of people who live together and love each other.
Parents are Mummy and Papa who take care of us.
Grandparents (Dadi and Dadu) are our parents' parents.
Siblings are our brothers and sisters.
Uncles, aunts, and cousins are our relatives and extended family.
We should love, respect, and help our family members.

slides.inSimpleWords: Family is the most important thing. Love your family and they will always be there for you.

image.alt: What We Learned — My Family

subject: The World Around Us
title: Priya Discovers Water
hook: Learn where water comes from and how we use it every day.

characters.name: Priya
characters.role: curious girl who loves to play with water

characters.name: Well Uncle
characters.role: village well keeper who shows where water comes from

slides.title: Water
slides.storyContext: Priya wakes up in the morning and drinks a glass of water. She splashes water on her face.
slides.inSimpleWords: Water is clear and wet. We use it every day.

image.alt: Water — Water

slides.title: Where Does Water Come From?
slides.storyContext: Priya watches Mummy fill the bucket from the tap. 'Where does this water come from?' she asks. Mummy smiles and says, 'Come, let me show you. Water comes from the river, wells, and the rain from the sky. It is brought to our homes through pipes.'
slides.inSimpleWords: Water comes from rivers, wells, rain, and pipes that bring it to our homes.

image.alt: Where Does Water Come From? — Water

slides.title: Rain - Water from the Sky
slides.storyContext: It is monsoon time. Priya runs to the window and watches rain fall. Pitter-patter! Pitter-patter! She sees puddles forming in the courtyard. Ravi jumps in the puddles. Mummy explains, 'The rain brings us fresh water from the clouds.'

points.label: What is rain?
points.text: Rain is water that falls from clouds in the sky.

points.label: When does it rain?
points.text: Rain falls most during monsoon season (June to September in India) and sometimes in other seasons too.

slides.inSimpleWords: Rain is water that falls from the sky and helps plants grow.

image.alt: Rain - Water from the Sky — Water

slides.title: Rivers and Wells - Water Underground and Flowing
slides.storyContext: Priya's family goes to the river near the village. She sees water flowing fast. 'This water flows all the way to the sea,' Mummy says. Later, Well Uncle shows her the well. He pulls up a bucket and says, 'Deep under the ground, there is water that fills this well.'

points.label: Rivers
points.text: Rivers are flowing water that comes from mountains and rain. They flow to the sea.

points.label: Wells
points.text: Wells are holes dug deep into the ground to bring up water that is stored below.

slides.inSimpleWords: Rivers and wells are natural sources of water that people have used for thousands of years.

image.alt: Rivers and Wells - Water Underground and Flowing — Water

slides.title: Water in Our Homes
slides.storyContext: Mummy turns the tap in the kitchen. Water flows out. 'We have water pipes in our house,' she tells Priya. 'This water is cleaned at a water treatment plant before it comes to our home through these pipes.'

points.label: Taps
points.text: Taps bring clean water into our homes from water pipes.

points.label: We need it
points.text: We use this water for drinking, cooking, washing, and cleaning.

slides.inSimpleWords: Pipes bring clean water to our homes so we can drink and wash.

image.alt: Water in Our Homes — Water

slides.title: How We Use Water
slides.storyContext: Priya's day is full of water! She drinks water for breakfast, washes her hands before eating, takes a bath, brushes her teeth, and helps Mummy wash vegetables in the kitchen. At night, she waters the plants in the garden with Dadi.

points.label: Drinking
points.text: We drink water to stay healthy and strong.

points.label: Washing
points.text: We wash our bodies, clothes, and dishes with water.

points.label: Cooking
points.text: We use water to cook rice, dal, and other foods.

points.label: Plants
points.text: We water plants and gardens so they grow.

slides.inSimpleWords: We use water for drinking, washing, cooking, and watering plants.

image.alt: How We Use Water — Water

slides.title: Animals and Plants Need Water
slides.storyContext: At the park, Priya sees cows drinking from a trough. A dog runs to a pool of water. Birds come to the bird bath to drink and splash. In the garden, Dadi pours water on the jasmine flowers and they smell sweet. Without water, plants and animals cannot live.

points.label: Animals drink water
points.text: Cows, dogs, birds, and all animals need to drink water to live.

points.label: Plants need water
points.text: Trees, flowers, and grass need water to grow and stay green.

slides.inSimpleWords: All living things - plants, animals, and people - need water to live.

image.alt: Animals and Plants Need Water — Water

slides.title: A Day with Water
slides.storyContext: Priya counts all the times she uses water in one day: morning bath (1), breakfast drink (2), washing hands (3), school (4), coming home and playing (5), cooking with Mummy (6), watering plants (7), evening bath (8), night brush (9). She realizes water is everywhere!

example.problem: Priya uses water 9 times in a day. If she saves 1 glass of water each time by not wasting it, how many glasses can she save in one day?
example.solution: Priya can save 9 glasses of water in one day! That is enough water for a plant to drink for many days.

slides.inSimpleWords: Water is part of everything we do - we use it many times every day.

image.alt: A Day with Water — Water

slides.title: Don't Waste Water!
slides.storyContext: Mummy teaches Priya: 'Water is precious. Not everyone has clean water to drink. We must not waste it.' Priya decides to close the tap tightly, take quick baths, and be careful not to spill water when drinking.

example.problem: How can you save water at home? Think of 3 ways you can help.
example.solution: Sample answers: 1. Close the tap while brushing teeth, 2. Take quick showers, 3. Don't let water run while washing vegetables, 4. Collect water and use it to water plants.

slides.inSimpleWords: Save water because many people do not have enough clean water. Use it carefully.

image.alt: Don't Waste Water! — Water

slides.title: What We Learned

points.text: Water comes from rain, rivers, wells, and underground sources.
Water is brought to our homes through pipes and taps.
We use water for drinking, washing, cooking, and watering plants.
All animals and plants need water to live.
Water is precious and we should not waste it.
Saving water helps everyone have enough clean water.

slides.inSimpleWords: Water is life. Use it wisely and share it with everyone.

image.alt: What We Learned — Water

subject: The World Around Us
title: Ravi's Day and Night
hook: Learn why we have day and night, and what happens in each.

characters.name: Ravi
characters.role: boy who observes the sun and moon

characters.name: Dadi
characters.role: grandmother who explains the sun and moon

characters.name: Moon
characters.role: the moon that watches the night

slides.title: Day and Night
slides.storyContext: Ravi wakes up in the morning when the sun rises. He goes to sleep at night when the moon comes out.
slides.inSimpleWords: Day is when the sun is in the sky and it is bright. Night is when it is dark and we sleep.

image.alt: Day and Night — Day and Night

slides.title: The Sun Brings the Day
slides.storyContext: Ravi opens his eyes and sees sunlight coming through the window. The birds are singing. 'Dadi, why is it so bright?' he asks. Dadi smiles and says, 'The sun is up, beta! When the sun rises in the morning, it is day. The sun gives us light and heat.'
slides.inSimpleWords: During the day, the sun shines and gives us light and warmth.

image.alt: The Sun Brings the Day — Day and Night

slides.title: What Happens During the Day?
slides.storyContext: Ravi's daily activities show what happens in the day. He wakes up at 6 AM when it is bright. He goes to school, plays outside, and can see everything clearly. Mummy hangs wet clothes to dry in the sun. Dadi sits outside and works in her vegetable garden. At noon, the sun is very bright and hot. Everyone can see very clearly and work outside.

points.label: Light
points.text: During the day, the sun gives us bright light so we can see.

points.label: Heat
points.text: The sun gives us warmth and heat during the day.

points.label: Work and play
points.text: People work, study, and play during the day because there is light.

slides.inSimpleWords: During the day, the sun is bright and warm. We can see and do things.

image.alt: What Happens During the Day? — Day and Night

slides.title: The Sun Moves Across the Sky
slides.storyContext: Ravi watches the sun all day. In the morning (sunrise), the sun comes from the east and is low in the sky. At noon (midday), the sun is very high above his head. In the afternoon, the sun moves to the west and starts to go down. By evening (sunset), the sun is very red and low in the sky again.

points.label: Sunrise
points.text: The sun rises in the east in the morning (around 6 AM).

points.label: Noon
points.text: The sun is highest in the sky at noon (around 12 PM).

points.label: Sunset
points.text: The sun sets in the west in the evening (around 6 PM).

slides.inSimpleWords: The sun moves across the sky from morning to evening.

image.alt: The Sun Moves Across the Sky — Day and Night

slides.title: Evening Comes - The Sun Goes Down
slides.storyContext: At 5 PM, Ravi notices the sky is becoming orange and red. Dadi says, 'Look, beta, the sun is going down. Soon it will be night.' The sun becomes smaller and disappears below the horizon. It gets darker and darker. The birds fly back to their nests. Mummy lights a lamp.

points.label: Sunset
points.text: At sunset, the sun disappears below the horizon.

points.label: Darkness
points.text: After sunset, it becomes dark outside and we cannot see clearly.

points.label: Twilight
points.text: Just after sunset, the sky is purple and orange for a short time. This is called twilight.

slides.inSimpleWords: When the sun sets, it gets dark and day becomes night.

image.alt: Evening Comes - The Sun Goes Down — Day and Night

slides.title: Night Arrives - The Moon and Stars Come Out
slides.storyContext: At 7 PM, it is completely dark. Ravi runs to the window and sees the moon in the sky! 'Dadi! The moon!' he shouts. Dadi comes and points, 'Yes, beta. When the sun goes away, the moon and stars come out. The moon gives us soft light in the night.'

points.label: The moon
points.text: The moon rises at night and gives us soft, white light.

points.label: The stars
points.text: Stars are tiny bright points of light that shine at night.

points.label: Darkness
points.text: Without the moon and stars, the night would be very dark.

slides.inSimpleWords: When the sun goes down, the moon and stars shine in the night sky.

image.alt: Night Arrives - The Moon and Stars Come Out — Day and Night

slides.title: What Happens at Night?
slides.storyContext: At night, many things are different. Animals sleep - birds are in their nests, cows are in the shed, dogs lie down. Ravi's family eats dinner by lamplight. Ravi's eyes get tired. At 8 PM, Dadi tells stories and Ravi yawns. By 9 PM, Ravi is in bed and falls asleep. The streets are quiet. Shops close. Mummy and Papa also go to sleep. Only the moon and stars watch over the sleeping village.

points.label: Rest and sleep
points.text: At night, people and animals rest and sleep.

points.label: Darkness
points.text: Night is dark. We need lamps, lights, and candles to see.

points.label: Quiet
points.text: Night is usually quiet and peaceful.

slides.inSimpleWords: At night, it is dark and quiet. People and animals sleep.

image.alt: What Happens at Night? — Day and Night

slides.title: Ravi's Day and Night Timetable
slides.storyContext: Ravi writes down what happens at different times: 6 AM - Wake up, sunrise, bright light; 8 AM - Go to school; 12 PM - Noon, sun is highest, very hot; 3 PM - Come home from school; 6 PM - Sunset, sun goes down; 7 PM - Night, moon and stars come out; 9 PM - Go to sleep; 12 AM - Midnight, darkest time.

example.problem: Ravi sleeps at 9 PM and wakes up at 6 AM. How many hours does he sleep? (Count: 9 PM to 6 AM = 9 hours)
example.solution: Ravi sleeps for 9 hours. This is good sleep for a first-grader who needs rest to grow and learn.

slides.inSimpleWords: A day has 24 hours - about 12 hours of day and 12 hours of night.

image.alt: Ravi's Day and Night Timetable — Day and Night

slides.title: Day or Night Activities?
slides.storyContext: Dadi plays a game with Ravi. She says an activity and Ravi must say whether it is a day activity or a night activity: 'Play cricket? Going to school? Sleeping? Eating lunch? Looking at stars? Drinking milk before bed?'

example.problem: Sort these into Day and Night: playing with friends, brushing teeth, eating dinner, going to school, sleeping, seeing the sun, watching the moon, having breakfast
example.solution: Day: playing with friends, eating breakfast, going to school, seeing the sun, eating lunch. Night: brushing teeth (before sleep), sleeping, watching the moon.

slides.inSimpleWords: Some things we do during the day and some things at night.

image.alt: Day or Night Activities? — Day and Night

slides.title: What We Learned

points.text: Day is when the sun is in the sky and it is bright.
The sun rises in the east in the morning and sets in the west in the evening.
During the day, we can see clearly and do work and play.
Night is when the sun is gone and it is dark.
The moon and stars shine at night and give soft light.
At night, people and animals rest and sleep.
A day and night together make 24 hours - one full day.

slides.inSimpleWords: Day and night happen because the Earth spins. The sun lights the day, and the moon lights the night.

image.alt: What We Learned — Day and Night
